title: World Labs opens Atlas world-model apps and developer APIs
summary: World Labs is opening Viewfinder and Chisel alongside Atlas APIs, letting developers reconstruct, edit and export explorable 3D worlds.
body:
## From world-model demo to developer surface

World Labs has opened access to a set of applications and APIs built around Atlas, its world model for reconstructing and generating three-dimensional environments. The launch includes Viewfinder, Chisel and developer endpoints that can be used directly by applications and agents.

Viewfinder turns a single image, or a set of images, into an explorable world and lets users move a virtual camera through reconstructed scenes. Chisel focuses on controllable scene construction: users can start from text or reference images, block out geometry and revise the layout through an agentic workflow.

World Labs also highlights tools for converting splats into meshes, relighting scenes and bringing generated worlds into existing creative software, including Blender. The company says developers can use the APIs behind the applications rather than being limited to a hosted demonstration.

## Why the API layer matters

World models are often presented as visual showcases, but production use depends on whether the output can be edited, queried and transferred into another pipeline. The combination of controllable geometry, camera-aware reconstruction and API access is therefore more consequential than a single rendered clip.

The target market spans games, visual effects, design, simulation and robotics research. Each has different requirements for geometric consistency, scene persistence and export formats. A visually convincing reconstruction that cannot survive later editing remains closer to a demo than a production asset.

## Why it matters

The release pushes spatial intelligence toward a tool layer that other agents can call. If Atlas can preserve structure across edits and integrate with established 3D workflows, it could reduce the cost of creating environments for games and simulation. The open question is whether its API outputs are reliable enough for repeatable production, rather than only compelling first-pass exploration.

**Uncle Cat take:** Opening Chisel’s API is more important than the showcase scenes because editable geometry, not camera movement, determines whether Atlas enters production pipelines.
title_zh: World Labs开放 Atlas 应用与开发者 API
summary_zh: World Labs围绕 Atlas 世界模型开放 Viewfinder、Chisel 及开发者接口，支持从图片重建可探索场景并编辑三维世界。
body_zh:
## 世界模型开始提供开发者入口

World Labs 开放了一组基于 Atlas 世界模型的应用和 API。此次发布包括 Viewfinder、Chisel，以及可以直接被应用和智能体调用的开发者接口。

Viewfinder 可以把单张图片或多张图片转换为可探索的三维世界，用户随后能在重建场景中移动虚拟摄像机。Chisel 则更强调可控建模：用户可以从文字或参考图开始搭建场景，通过智能体工作流调整结构和布局。

World Labs 还提供把 splat 转换成网格、重新布光，以及将生成世界带入现有创作软件的工具，包括 Blender。公司表示，开发者可以直接调用这些应用背后的 API，而不必停留在托管演示层面。

## API层决定能否进入生产

世界模型经常以视觉效果展示，但真正用于生产，关键在于输出能否继续编辑、被程序读取，并转入其他工作流。因此，可控几何、基于摄像机的场景重建和 API 访问，比单个漂亮渲染画面更有意义。

潜在用户包括游戏、影视特效、设计、仿真和机器人研究。不过，这些领域对几何一致性、场景持久化和导出格式的要求各不相同。一旦重建结果无法继续修改，它就更像一次演示，而不是可交付的生产资产。

## 为什么重要

这次发布把空间智能推向可被其他智能体调用的工具层。如果 Atlas 能在多次编辑后保持结构稳定，并融入成熟的 3D 工作流，它有望降低游戏和仿真环境的制作成本。尚未解决的问题是：API 输出是否足够稳定，能否支持重复生产，而不只是一次性的探索体验。

**猫叔判断：** Chisel开放 API 比展示场景更重要，因为能否编辑几何体，才决定 Atlas 会不会进入真正的生产管线。
cat_take_zh: Chisel开放API比演示画面重要，能否编辑几何才决定Atlas能否量产
cat_take_en: Chisel’s API matters more than showcase renders because editable geometry decides whether Atlas becomes a production asset.
